title = "Drinking Battle with My Senior"

<p>It was Senior Min-ah.</p><p>While I was meeting with the company’s representative and discussing matters, the directors were also present—and there, dressed in a suit, sat Noona Min-ah.</p><p>I relayed the Association President’s message to the representative as-is, and the representative said they’d remain loyal as long as the Association delivered on the promised privileges.</p><p>In any case, my aide had handled most of the work, and I was too distracted by Noona Min-ah to focus properly.</p><p>I’d always assumed Noona Min-ah wasn’t particularly interested in money and would stay at the Association forever, so the news that she’d transferred to a company came as quite a shock.</p><p>After the meeting ended, I sent the aides away first and followed Senior Min-ah.</p><p>“Senior.”</p><p>“People really are unpredictable… Here I was, weaker than you back then, and now you’re an S-rank Hunter and even the Vice President of the Association? I heard the rumors—is it true you decked the former Intelligence Chief?”</p><p>“It wasn’t a full-on punch, just a slap… No, that’s not the point. When did you leave the Association? Was there a problem?”</p><p>“A problem? Nah. I just quit because it stopped being fun.”</p><p>“···.”</p><p>I’d forgotten after all this time.</p><p>This noona was always like this.</p><p>Even as a long-range A-rank Hunter who primarily used a bow, if the attackers were being slow, she’d toss the bow aside, draw her sword, and start beating monsters to a pulp.</p><p>The only reason she’d picked up a bow in the first place was because she hated getting blood on her clothes.</p><p>“After that day, I thought you’d quit being a Hunter for good. How’d you end up coming back?”</p><p>“Well… yeah.”</p><p>“Let’s grab a meal sometime when you’re free. Wait, no—you’re the Vice President now, so *you* should treat *me*.”</p><p>“Sure thing.”</p><p>After exchanging brief greetings with Noona Min-ah, we swapped numbers and I left the building.</p><p>I hadn’t been in touch, so I hadn’t realized—her number had changed too.</p><p>***</p><p>“Over here!”</p><p>“Ah, Senior.”</p><p>A month after meeting Noona Min-ah, I got a call from her.</p><p>When she said let’s drink, I assumed it’d be at a regular bar. Of course, I should’ve known better.</p><p>This noona had always been a severe Dropz addict.</p><p>There were times back then when the party leader, hyung, had caught her smuggling Dropz into the Gate and confiscated them all.</p><p>She was always clever about it, though—hiding Dropz in her canteen and drinking it like water.</p><p>Of course, as an A-rank Hunter, she had an incredible tolerance for alcohol, so even Dropz didn’t get her drunk easily.</p><p>Whenever a Gate turned out to be harder than expected, she’d pull out a hidden flask from her coat and take a swig. Once, purely out of curiosity, I’d asked her why she drank it.</p><p>He said something like he’d rather die drunk than sober…</p><p>Since it was the weekend, Yu-na and Echo took Lion to Echo’s castle.</p><p>Echo had been piling up work lately, so he’d been returning to his castle about once a week.</p><p>The problem was that Echo said he got lonely by himself, so he ended up taking Yu-na and Lion with him.</p><p>Or rather, Yu-na seemed to enjoy spending time at Echo’s castle, so she didn’t mind taking Lion along.</p><p>Ji-hyeon went with them too, and when I asked what they did there, she said watching magic was fun.</p><p>Well, it *was* real supernatural power—nothing like mere stage magic—so it made sense it’d be entertaining.</p><p>Since Lion was born there, he seemed comfortable and settled in well even at Echo’s castle.</p><p>He’s my son, but I have a feeling he’s going to grow up to be something extraordinary.</p><p>In the end, if I wanted to drink Drops, I’d have to do it either in private or at an illegal bar. But if the vice president of the Hunter Association showed up at an illegal bar in broad daylight, some Hunter would recognize me, and I’d end up on the front page of the papers. So we decided to eat out and then head to my sister Min-a’s place for drinks.</p><p>“Are snacks okay? Or do you need more?”</p><p>“I’m fine, but what about you, sunbae?”</p><p>“What are you talking about… You can’t even hold your liquor as well as I can. Do you have any idea how many times I’ve had to carry you home after you passed out?”</p><p>Back in the day, Min-a noona had gotten me drunk a few times, and I’d pretended to black out.</p><p>It wasn’t like I’d actually lost consciousness—I’d just known that if I drank any more, I *would* pass out, so I’d faked it on purpose.</p><p>Back then, Min-a noona could outdrink me by a mile, but that was when I was still weak… back when I was just a human. Now that I was half-monster, I could confidently say there wasn’t a single human alive who could beat me in a drinking contest.</p><p>“It’s been ages since it was just the two of us drinking. You used to beg me to buy you alcohol all the time.”</p><p>“That was Woo-hyeok hyung, not me… I’ve never once asked *you* to buy me drinks.”</p><p>“Oh, really? What’s Woo-hyeok up to these days?”</p><p>“As far as I know, he’s working as an instructor.”</p><p>We drank and reminiscence about old times.</p><p>Min-a noona was one of the few people who knew about my early days as a Hunter—back before even Hye-na knew me.</p><p>I’d been recklessly charging into Gates without a care, until I got badly burned once, after which I’d only stuck to low-rank Gates and lived like a shut-in.</p><p>Back then, I never could’ve imagined that one day I’d overcome my past trauma and be sitting here, sharing a drink with her like this.</p><p>“Don’t you keep in touch with the others?”</p><p>“We still talk now and then. Most of them got married, had kids, and now they either work as instructors or quit being Hunters altogether and switched careers.”</p><p>“Well, if they’re married, that makes sense.”</p><p>Three empty Drop bottles were already lying on the floor.</p><p>Min-a noona opened the fridge, and it was packed full of Drop.</p><p>“How many bottles do you drink in a day…?”</p><p>“I don’t drink much by myself. I just buy them in bulk for when I get the craving before bed. It’s a hassle to go out and buy one every time I want some.”</p><p>“….”</p><p>***</p><p>“Ungh? So, so, listen to me….”</p><p>“I’m listening….”</p><p>“I just don’t get why the Association is trying to absorb private companies….”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Wouldn’t it be prettier if we all just kept each other in check like the old days? And I’m not just saying this because I switched to the private sector, okay?”</p><p>“Did you know you’ve said that exact line more than ten times now?”</p><p>“So, so, just listen to me, okay?”</p><p>“Huuu….”</p><p>It was only 5 PM, but the floor was already littered with fifteen empty Drop bottles, and Min-a noona was thoroughly drunk.</p><p>She was stuck in the worst of her drunken habits—repeating the same thing over and over.</p><p>And I was partly to blame for this.</p><p>Now that Drop barely had any effect on me, it just tasted like a faintly alcoholic beverage. I’d absentmindedly poured her glass after glass, and Min-a noona, trying to keep up with my pace, had downed them too quickly and gotten wasted.</p><p>“You should go to sleep now.”</p><p>“Huh? I’m not drunk.”</p><p>The moment you tell a drunk person, “You’re drunk,” the gates of hell swing open.</p><p>With drunk people, you have to soothe them by insisting they’re *not* drunk.</p><p>“No, I think *I’m* the one who’s drunk.”</p><p>“Oh? Well… can’t be helped, then.”</p><p>She bought it.</p><p>This was the trick—gradually acknowledging their drunkenness while gently coaxing them along.</p><p>If I wanted to avoid the legendary worst-case drunken behavior I’d only heard rumors about, I needed to escape *now*.</p><p>“Aren’t you tired?”</p><p>“Hmm?”</p><p>“I’m tired….”</p><p>Min-a noona started muttering with completely unfocused eyes.</p><p>“Uh, then go to sleep… I should get going. Let’s meet up again sometime for a meal. Today was fun. See you later.”</p><p>As I stood up to leave, Min-a noona started taking off her clothes.</p><p>This was the legendary drunken behavior Woo-hyuk hyung had told me about.</p><p>Woo-hyuk hyung was one of the few people with a tolerance as high as Min-a noona’s, so he was the only one who’d ever witnessed her at her absolute worst—blackout drunk.</p><p>According to him, when Min-a noona was completely wasted, she’d say she was too tired to do anything but shower and sleep… and then start stripping.</p><p>Hyuk-hyung would always flee the scene at times like that.</p><p>He said that when he was completely drunk, it was harder to tell he was drunk, so right now, Mina noona was definitely wasted.</p><p>“I’m going to shower. Wanna join me?”</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291641" loading="lazy">
</p><p>“Goodbye.”</p><p>I kicked the door open and bolted out of there.</p><p>“Ahaha…”</p><p>I couldn’t help but laugh on my way home.</p><p>Maybe it was just fun to drink with a close noona after so long.</p><p>For some reason, I didn’t feel even a hint of lust toward Mina noona.</p><p>The walk home was a long one, but I passed the time by replaying the conversations we’d had over drinks.</p><p>I might end up seeing Mina noona often from now on.</p><p>Since the private Hunter company she worked for was being absorbed by the Hunter Association, they’d already promised her a high-ranking position. It seemed likely she’d be appointed as the head of a key department.</p><p>Given that she’d originally been active in Incheon, she might even be assigned as the branch director there.</p><p>Her skills were more than enough—no one would dare object.</p><p>***</p><p>“I’m home.”</p><p>“You’re late.”</p><p>Na-hyeon was sitting on the sofa in her pajamas, watching TV.</p><p>“Yeah, I had to handle some work at a private company, then ran into an old sunbae and ended up having a drink.”</p><p>“Mom and Ji-hyeon are coming in two days, so it’s just the two of us until then.”</p><p>“Huh? Oh, yeah, I guess so.”</p><p>Swoosh</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291642" loading="lazy">
</p><p>Na-hyeon stood up from the sofa, slowly stripping off her pajamas as she approached me.</p><p>“Then… we can spend the whole night together, just the two of us.”</p><p>“Yeah… but what about work tomorrow?”</p><p>“Didn’t you work all weekend last week too? Se-rin and I agreed to split the shifts this week. I took the day off tomorrow.”</p><p>“I still have to go in…”</p><p>Na-hyeon gently traced the collar of my shirt and whispered,</p><p>“You can go a few days without sleep, right?”</p><p>“···.”</p><p>At this rate, I really might end up impregnating every single woman in my family.</p><p>Then my only options would be to flee the country or beg Echo to use magic to keep everyone from finding out.</p><p>But what could I do?</p><p>This was my own doing.</p>
